text:
maya: Running long chat sessions (~40-60k tokens) on Dedicated and seeing steady KV resident memory growth (~6-8GB over 6h). Hosted runs same workload but usually plateaus. Private on-prem shows intermittent spikes and fragmentation. Opening thread to sync.

jon: Which model + kernel + batching config? repro?

maya: Model rw-7b-v2-fp16 (quantized path on Dedicated). Kernel mix: fast-attn where available, fallback to cuBLAS for some layers. Batch size per request 1-2 (streaming chat), reuse/prefix caching enabled. Repro script (very small):

```bash
# repro.sh - run a long chat loop to exercise KV reuse and paging
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-infer.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt": "long-context-step", "max_new_tokens": 32, "stream": false}' >/dev/null
  sleep 0.2
done
```

maya: Quick VM snapshot (dedicated node):

```
$ ps aux | grep inferd
redwood   4281  8.6 45.2 2876540 185432 ? Sl 08:12 12:34 /usr/bin/inferd --kv-enabled
$ pmap -x 4281 | tail -n 5
total kB  370000000  120000000  250000000
```

sheraz: Do we have perf / pmap / smaps traces? Sounds like pagefaults and retained anon pages. Hosted likely has different vm tunables (swappiness / madvise) which explains plateauing there.

maya: I ran a 30m perf capture. Top of heap profile shows a lot of pinned frames from kv allocator and repeated "madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)" falling through. Snippet:

```
# pprof top-like pseudo
39.2%  inferd  [anon:kvcache] malloc_consolidate
17.8%          kv_alloc_frame
12.1%          memcpy (token copy)
7.4%           page_fault_handler
```

liz: Could this be jemalloc decay / tcache settings? Also check /proc/sys/vm/swappiness and THP. Hosted probably has swappiness=10 and THP=never. Dedicated defaults might be different.

maya: Confirmed: dedicated node had vm.swappiness=60, THP=always. On Hosted we have swappiness=10, THP=never. Quick test: lowered swappiness to 10 on a staging dedicated -> resident growth flattened but fragmentation still visible.

dave: NUMA could be amplifying fragmentation on on-prem GPUs (private). If allocator and mmap placement differ, we can get scattered page residency causing high RSS with lots of noncontiguous mappings. Also small writes from streaming batches cause many tiny allocations.

maya: I tried enabling dynamic batching merging so runtime aggregates small token writes into 8-token chunks before committing KV frames. That reduced number of KV allocations and memcpy calls. Result: growth rate dropped ~60% in 2h test. Logs:

```
[2026-02-10T14:12:01Z] kv: merge-window=8 applied, merged_frames=2400, avg_frame_bytes=8192
[2026-02-10T15:12:01Z] kv: resident_growth_mb=+120 -> baseline
```

jon: Good. Action items I propose: 1) standardize vm.swappiness=10 and set THP=never on Dedicated images; 2) add jemalloc tuning (decay time, background thread) to Dedicated profile; 3) add long-context perf e2e to our CI that runs merged-batching + streaming mix; 4) add alert: kv_resident_derivative > 50MB/hr for 3h.

sheraz: Also add runtime knobs: `kv.cache_eviction_margin` (percentage) and `kv.max_pinned_frames`. We should A/B quantized kernel combos: quantized CPU/GPU kernels tend to pin more pages for KV storage.

liz: For Private (on-prem) add NUMA-aware mmap policy (mbind) when we detect GPU local memory domains. Also include an ops doc to run `numastat -p <pid>` and `cat /proc/<pid>/smaps` during repro.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job started for swappiness change on staging-dedicated-1 (job id canary-987).

jon: Can someone run the repro.sh on a Dedicated node and paste `cat /proc/<pid>/smaps | egrep "Anon|Swap|Rss|VmFlags"` plus `perf script` output? That will help pinpoint whether pages are truly pinned or just not returned to OS by allocator.

maya: Kicking off run on ded-3 now. Will paste smaps + perf when complete (~40m). I'll also open infra PR to unify swappiness/THP and a runtime PR to expose `kv.max_pinned_frames` and default `merge-window=8` for streaming workloads.

jon: Thanks — let's aim to have the infra PR + runtime patch in canary by EOD so we can validate with overnight long-context job.

maya: will do.
